name: Converge
label: Deathwish
lede: Two teenagers in Salem, Massachusetts, a four-track, and 35 years of building the loudest, most careful chaos in hardcore, right down to the artwork and the studio.

eras.title: Salem kids with a four-track
eras.text: Converge starts as teenagers in Salem, Massachusetts, covering hardcore and metal, then learning to write their own. By 1995 they have a second guitarist, a self-funded debut, and a studio that is really just Kurt Ballou with a tape machine.

years.h: Jacob Bannon and Kurt Ballou start Converge in Salem, Massachusetts
years.p: [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]] and [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] begin with covers of hardcore punk and heavy metal songs, with [[Jeff Feinburg|61a3233a-63dd-4ae2-ac08-68ac9994735b]] and [[Damon Bellorado|fd79eaf6-1179-4aa4-8fcd-b535a56cc94e]] soon in the line-up.
years.xp: Exclaim! reports the name was picked because it was not a hardcore cliche. The band recorded early demos on a four-track and began playing shows in mid-1991, per Wikipedia. Exclaim! also credits the Gravel demo, cut at West Sound Studio in Londonderry, New Hampshire, and released on cassette.

years.h: [[Aaron Dalbec|5ea0f2e5-66d0-48ce-82d5-9c85d2fa4c39]] joins as second guitarist, making Converge a five-piece
years.p: Dalbec, met through the Boston hardcore scene, adds a second guitar to Bannon, Ballou, Feinburg and Bellorado.

years.h: Halo in a Haystack: a debut Bannon paid for with nursing home wages
years.p: Bannon funded the first album himself, then decided he would control every piece of Converge artwork after this one.
years.xp: Exclaim! puts the release in spring 1994 on Earthmaker and Stolnacke; Wikipedia gives August 10, 1994 and a vinyl pressing of 1,000 copies. Bannon was unhappy with the record's art, which is why he took over the visuals for good.

years.h: Unloved and Weeded Out 7-inch shows the band getting sharper
years.p: The 1995 seven-inch is a clear step up from Halo in a Haystack, after a stretch when college nearly broke the band apart.
years.xp: Exclaim! says members were at different colleges and the band came close to ending until the distance, about five hours between Montreal and Boston, proved workable. The songs were later collected on a 2003 compilation of the same name.

years.cap: The metalcore band Converge playing at Neumo's in Seattle, Washington. · Wikimedia
years.h: Ballou starts recording bands as GodCity Studio
years.p: Kurt Ballou names his small recording setup GodCity, after a [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]] song. It becomes where nearly every Converge album is made.
years.xp: Exclaim! says Ballou joked his ultimate business goal was maybe having his own phone line someday. The current Salem location opened in 2003.

eras.title: A bassist in the bushes
eras.text: The band hits a first real stride on record, swaps bassists twice, and gets noticed by Equal Vision. By April 1998 they have a label, a producer from Today Is the Day, and a new bassist from Jesuit.

years.h: Petitioning the Empty Sky puts Converge on the map
years.p: The Ferret Records release goes out as a seven-inch and then a longer CD, with "The Saddest Day" becoming a set staple.
years.xp: A radio session captured for the reissue shows Bannon bleeding after a mic stand hit. The band also covered Twisted Sister's "Burn in Hell", which Bannon treated as truly heavy rather than a joke.

years.h: [[Stephen Brodsky|a0ff602c-7f3e-472d-8786-953da6cd7591]] replaces Jeff Feinburg on bass
years.p: Brodsky, of [[Cave In|f3c95ad4-215b-4519-8660-84c9f467da05]], takes over bass. Ballou pulled him out of high school to record, and he hid in bushes from truant officers.

years.h: Equal Vision's Steve Reddy sees Converge headline Northampton
years.p: At the Really Loud Music Festival, Reddy is struck by the crowd, where the nerds and emo kids were all fighting each other; Equal Vision Records signs them in July.
years.xp: The signing came out of that single festival set, per Exclaim!. Equal Vision's first move was to reissue Petitioning the Empty Sky, which came out on January 20, 1998 with three live radio tracks added.

years.h: When Forever Comes Crashing: first Equal Vision album
years.p: Produced by Steve Austin of Today Is the Day, it is Brodsky's only full-length with Converge.
years.xp: The band recorded at GodCity from December 22, 1997 to January 3, 1998, per Wikipedia. Equal Vision reissued it in 2005 with bonus tracks and new artwork by Aaron Turner of Isis.

years.h: [[Nate Newton|5279c1b0-6751-4836-9c71-9abd227bd209]] of Jesuit takes over bass
years.p: Newton joins part-time while still in Jesuit, which broke up in 1999, and stays for good.

eras.title: The four-piece and the record kids would hate
eras.text: Ben Koller arrives, Newton starts writing, Bannon founds Deathwish, and Converge makes Jane Doe in three studios over about three years. Dalbec leaves as it comes out, and the band that remains is the one still touring.

years.h: [[Ben Koller|b6fdd346-b9e8-449a-9105-612d3722503f]] joins on drums, at age 19
years.p: After Bellorado left in early 1999 and John DiGiorgio filled in briefly, Koller, a Converge fan, plays his first show with them at a Chinese restaurant.
years.xp: Ballou knew Koller from Force Fed Glass and Blue/Green Heart. Exclaim! quotes Koller calling it a Mark Wahlberg in Rock Star thing. Koller later formed [[Mutoid Man|d6c8e477-7221-47be-bab3-fe6980cf4284]] with Brodsky.

years.cap: Converge performing live at Roadburn Festival 2018 · Wikimedia
years.h: Bannon and Tre McCarthy turn Deathwish Inc. into a real label
years.p: The two start putting out records after a late-1999 decision to make it a business; the first release, in 2001, is a Converge split with Hellchild.
years.xp: Bannon described the aim as a pro-band environment where artists are treated the way they would want to be. Wikipedia says the label now lists over 240 releases from 120-plus bands, and Converge has the most.

years.h: Deeper the Wound: Deathwish release number one
years.p: A split between Converge and Hellchild, with a demo, a Depeche Mode cover and live tracks from Converge.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the release to April 23, 2001; Exclaim! describes the Converge side.

years.cap: Jane Doe, cover art by Jacob Bannon
years.h: Jane Doe: Converge's breakthrough album
years.p: Recorded at Q Division, GodCity and Fort Apache, it is the first with Newton and Koller and the last with Dalbec.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports the album cost about $11,000 and was recorded to six reels of two-inch tape. At Q Division, Newton recalls James Taylor, next door, sending his engineer over to complain about the noise. Bannon recorded vocals in the dark at Fort Apache, alone.

Bannon says the lyrics came from a dissolving relationship. He recalled to Exclaim! that early press was overwhelmingly negative, but Terrorizer named it album of the year for 2001. Decibel later ranked it first among the best metal albums of the 2000s. In October 2021, French model Audrey Marnay said she was the basis for the cover image, taken from a May 2001 Marie Claire Italy photograph.

years.big: A hardcore record the kids would hate
q: a hardcore record the kids were going to hate
years.h: Newton and Koller write a record for the kids to hate
years.p: With Newton writing full songs for the first time, Converge set out to make Jane Doe less friendly than what hardcore expected.
years.xp: Newton contributed "The Broken Vow" and "Heaven in Her Arms" as complete songs, which shifted writing away from Ballou alone. Ballou has said Koller's arrival reinvigorated the band.

q: The label were pissed. They hated it.
years.h: Bannon's cover art has no Converge logo, and Equal Vision is furious
years.p: Bannon designed the Jane Doe cover himself, and the label was angry that the band's logo was missing.
years.xp: Exclaim! adds that Equal Vision also disliked the kinetic, hard-to-read booklet, but Bannon's vision held, and Reddy later said Converge knew what they wanted and delivered.

years.h: Aaron Dalbec plays his last show with Converge and the band becomes four
years.p: Dalbec, busy with [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]], is gone after the Jane Doe release; Ballou's stance was that any other change would end the band.
years.xp: Exclaim! says his last show was the album release around September 8. Wikipedia says he was asked to leave because of his commitment to Bane. Bannon says the recording felt like a quartet thing.

years.h: Ballou is laid off as a biomedical engineer the week Jane Doe comes out
years.p: The severance lets Ballou run Converge and GodCity full time.
years.xp: Exclaim! reports the layoff and that the pay let him grow the studio.

eras.title: Stitches, security guards and a label switch
eras.text: Converge tours hard, gets hurt, leaves Equal Vision for Epitaph, and makes You Fail Me and No Heroes at home in Salem.

years.h: Gainesvillefest ends with security swinging two-by-fours
years.p: A fight at the Florida festival was filmed and spread online, with bass player Nate Newton visible in the melee.
years.xp: Exclaim! says online guessing that Newton hit someone was wrong. Bannon recalled blood everywhere and Ballou calmly packing up his gear.

years.h: Converge leave Equal Vision Records for Epitaph Records
years.p: Epitaph offered the band respect for its independence, and Equal Vision was hurt.
years.xp: Exclaim! reports Equal Vision felt it was owed another album; Converge said the Petitioning reissue covered the contract. Reddy wrote that he was hurt but it was what it was.

years.h: You Fail Me: first Converge record to chart
years.p: Made at GodCity from March 2004, it reached number 171 on the Billboard 200 and adds a glockenspiel and a piano from a studio neighbor.
years.xp: Bannon titled it before writing anything, from a phrase he kept repeating in his journals. Matthew Ellard mixed it in three days because of repeated power outages. The band toured it with Cave In and Between the Buried and Me.

years.h: In Leipzig, Ballou's thrown guitar hits Bannon in the face
years.p: Six stitches for Jacob Bannon after Ballou tossed his guitar backward during a show.
years.xp: Newton told Exclaim! that they have all been to the hospital numerous times for this band. This was during the Aggressive Tendencies Tour with Terror.

years.h: No Heroes: Ballou records, engineers and mixes it all himself
years.p: The first Converge album with no outside producer, cut at GodCity and reaching number 151 on Billboard, per Exclaim!.
years.xp: Bannon shifted his lyrics toward "we" and "our" and away from "I". Exclaim! reports the band joked about calling it The Rapist, which worried the label about retail placement.

eras.title: Axe to Fall and the cult
eras.text: Converge becomes a family of bands and labels, sells out bigger rooms, and tours with cartoon metal band Dethklok. Side projects multiply: Old Man Gloom, Doomriders, Mutoid Man.

years.h: Axe to Fall: guests, choirs and a torn-finger guitar part
years.p: It has Neurosis's Steve Von Till on "Cruel Bloom" and reached number 74 on Billboard despite leaking two weeks early.
years.xp: Three songs came from a Verge-In side project with Cave In members, including "Effigy". Sean Martin, formerly of Hatebreed, recorded with a torn finger glued together. Newton also released Doomriders' Darkness Come Alive that year.

years.cap: Converge performing live at Roadburn Festival 2018 · Wikimedia
years.h: Converge open for Mastodon and Dethklok on the Metalocalypse tour
years.p: Adult Swim's late-2009 tour puts the band in front of arena-sized metal crowds, with High on Fire also on the bill.
years.xp: The "Axe to Fall" video debuted on MTV2's Headbangers Ball on November 7, per Wikipedia.

years.h: CONCULT01: the "On My Shield" 7-inch starts Converge's own series
years.p: A self-released single, sold on European tours and online, with a laser-etched sun on the B-side.
years.xp: CONCULT02 followed in 2011 as a split with Dropdead, and CONCULT03 with Napalm Death in 2012, which included a Wolverine Blues cover with [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] and Tomas Lindberg.

years.h: All We Love We Leave Behind peaks at number 70
years.p: The title track is about Bannon's dog Anna Belle, whom he missed while touring; Ballou called it a collection of singles.
years.xp: Vinyl was delayed by a Beatles box set, per Exclaim!. It charted higher than Axe to Fall.

eras.title: Blood Moon
eras.text: Converge stops just being a four-piece. A one-off Roadburn set turns into an ensemble with Chelsea Wolfe and eventually a full album, and Jane Doe gets its long-awaited live playback.

years.cap: Converge at the Eurockéennes of 2007 · Wikimedia
years.h: Roadburn 2016: Jane Doe in full, then Blood Moon with [[Chelsea Wolfe|60e8e938-365e-4429-a141-4c79eb49588d]]
years.p: For its 15th anniversary Converge play the album front to back in Tilburg, then return with Wolfe, Ben Chisholm, Stephen Brodsky and Steve Von Till for a slower set.
years.xp: The Blood Moon show came from a Roadburn invitation to do something special. Converge recorded arrangements at GodCity Studio for three days beforehand. Jane Live came out on March 3, 2017.

years.h: You Fail Me Redux remixes the 2004 album
years.p: Ballou remixed it to sit more comfortably between Jane Doe and No Heroes; Alan Douches remastered and Bannon repackaged it.

years.h: The Dusk in Us: the record after the longest break
years.p: It follows 2017's "I Can Tell You About Pain" seven-inch and ends with 18 songs recorded and 13 kept.
years.xp: Exclaim! says the four members had six kids in five years, and the mood of the record is uneasy and mid-paced. Ballou joked they were all equally unhappy with what ended up on the album.

years.h: Bloodmoon: I with Chelsea Wolfe, Chisholm and Brodsky
years.p: Made with Wolfe, Ben Chisholm and Stephen Brodsky as equal partners, not guests, and finished remotely during the pandemic.
years.xp: Bannon told Knotfest the material started about five years earlier, before the pandemic. It grew out of the 2016 Blood Moon shows.

eras.title: Two albums in one year
eras.text: After Bloodmoon, Converge go back to just the four of them and release a short album and a follow-up within months.

years.h: Love Is Not Enough: 31 minutes, the shortest Converge album
years.p: Recorded at GodCity with all guitar by Ballou; the first single came on November 19, 2025.
years.xp: Ballou said he barely played guitar on some of Bloodmoon, and this was about going back to the band's own material. Wikipedia lists Metacritic 84 and a 5 out of 5 from Kerrang!.

years.h: Hum of Hurt lands only four months later
years.p: The twelfth album was announced on April 1 with a cryptic billboard in Boston teasing the date.
years.xp: Details per Wikipedia; Revolver ran a feature on the band's urgency behind a second album in 2026.

sources.title: Exclaim!: When Forever Comes Crashing, A Full History of Converge
